newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Vols surge as stocks probe highs.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Vols surge as stocks probe highs.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. stock index options were pumped up in hectic morning trade as the underlying stock market extended gains and probed new highs, traders said.

The S&P 100 index .OEX rose above the 800 level for the first time, with heavy traffic in call options on the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE). Technology stocks again led the way up as they have in the last few sessions, traders said.
"They're not rallying, they're exploding," said Jesse Stamer of TradeNet, a CBOE designated primary market-maker.
The CBOE volatility index, which reflects implied volatilities for near-month OEX options, was up 1.25 points at 20.26 at 1100 CDT/1600 GMT.

VIX last week eroded to near 19 from above 22, after hovering above 20 for most of the year, as it generally tends to rise when stocks fall and decline when stocks rally. But the speed and the size of the market's gains in recent weeks were now fuelling interest from both call speculators and hedgers using puts, traders said.
"I think volatilities will continue to pick up if this market continues to go (higher)," Stamer said.

May 810 calls, with more than 9,700 contracts trading by 1100 CDT/1600 GMT, and May 820 calls, with more than 7,000 contracts, were the busiest OEX contracts. On the put side, while May 790 puts were the most active, with about 5,400 contracts changing hands.
Traders noted that the reversal today in VIX and a volume shift toward calls could be an early sign the market could see a near-term pullback.
Todd Salamone, a research analyst at Cincinnati-based Investment Research Institute, said near-term risk had clearly increased, although the longer-term outlook was positive.

"Now you're bumping up against some resistance areas as you people become more optimistic and complacent," he said, noting that VIX was still relatively low despite today's bounce. "That's when your risk becomes higher.
"But it takes a lot to jump into this momentum and call the exact short-term top," he added, however, stressing that the underlying trend was still for higher stock prices.
Stamer agreed: "Normally, I'd like to buy new highs."
He said many technology indices were close to making new highs and the market might first test those highs.
CBOE's technology index stood at 210.80 in late morning trade, up 4.06 points on the day and less than 10 points away from its late January highs.
Nasdaq 100 index .NDX was up 11.89 to 921.38, less than 20 points from its January highs.
A brokerage trader said he would turn short-term bearish if the market today closes on a weaker note.
"We saw a lot of strong closes last week," he said. "If we start seeing weaker closes, that could be signalling a change."
